The settled proposition of law, in our considered opinion, is that the order granting bail should reflect the judicial application of mind taking into consideration the well-known parameters including: r (i) The nature of the accusation weighing in the gravity and severity of the offence; (ii) The severity of punishment; (iii) The position or status of the accused, i.e. whether the accused can exercise influence on the victim and the witnesses or not; (iv) Likelihood of accused to approach or try to approach the victims/ witnesses; (v) Likelihood of accused absconding from proceedings; (vi) Possibility of accused tampering with evidence; (vii) Obstructing or attempting to obstruct the due course of justice; (viii) Possibility of repetition of offence if left out on bail; (ix) The prima facie satisfaction of the Rajeev Kumar vs State Of Himachal Pradesh on 4 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136364644/ 8 - 18 - 2024:HHC:4510 court in support of the charge including frivolity of the charge; (x) The different and distinct facts of each case and nature of substantive and corroborative evidence. . 12. We hasten to add that there can be several other relevant factors which, depending upon the peculiar facts and circumstances of a case, would be required to be kept in mind while granting or refusing bail to an accused. It may be difficult to illustrate all such circumstances, for there cannot be any straight jacket formula for exercising the discretionary jurisdiction vested in a Court under Sections 438 and 439 respectively of the Cr. PC, as the case may be." 9. In normal parlance, the general principle of law is that while considering the prayer for bail {pre-arrest bail or regular bail], a prima-facie opinion is to gathered as to whether reasonable grounds exist pointing towards the accusation or whether the accusation is frivolous and groundless with the object of either injuring or humiliating or whether a person has falsely roped in the crime needs to be tested in background of self-imposed restrains or the broad parameters mandated by law, as referred to herein above. - 19 - 2024 :HHC : 10 . This Court is also conscious of the f that as per the mandate of law, in Criminal Appeal No.3840 of 2023, titled as Saumya Churasia . versus Directorate of Enforcement, decided on 14.12.2023, while considering the prayer for bail, a Court is not required to weigh the evidence collected by the Investigating Agency meticulously , nonetheless, the Court should keep in mind the nature of accusation, nature of r evidence collected in support thereof, severity of punishment prescribed for alleged offences, character of accused, circumstances which are peculiar to the accused, the reasonable possibility of securing the presence of the accused during trial, reasonable apprehension of evidence being tampered with or any possibility of causing an inducement, threat or promise to the witnesses or the complainant or victim; and by carving out a balance between the liability of an accused vis--vis the societal interests of the Public/State at large. In this background, while testing the claim for bail, the Court, is required to form a prima-facie Rajeev Kumar vs State Of Himachal Pradesh on 4 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136364644/ 9 - 20 - 2024:HHC:4510 opinion in the context of the broad-parameters referred to above, without delving into the evidence on merits, as it may tend to prejudice the rights of the accused . as well as the prosecution.

However, this Court, vide orders dated 24.05.2024 passed in six cases dismissed their bail petitions, being devoid of any merit. 2. Now, remaining three accused [who are in custody] i.e. bail petitioners herein, namely, Rajeev Kumar; Kulveer Singh; and Jatinder Singh, have come up before this Court in Cr.MP(M) No.919 of 2024, Cr.MP(M) No.920 of 2024 and Cr.MP(M) No.921 of 2024; seeking regular bail under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal -3- 2024:HHC:4510 Procedure [referred to as 'Cr.P.C.], originating from same FIR i.e. No.14 of 2024, dated 20.01.2024, registered at Police Station, Nalagarh, District Solan [H.P.], under . Case set up by Mr. Nareshwar Singh Chandel, Learned Senior Counsel, assisted by Mr. Vinod Kumar Gupta and Mr. Ashok Kumar, learned counsel, is that Sandeep Kumar, son of Shri Rajinder Singh, R/o Village and Post Office, Bhattiyan, Tehsil Nalagarh, District Solan [H.P.], had submitted a complaint on 21.01.2024 to Head Constable Rakesh Kumar, No.42 that on 20.01.2024, while the complainant [Sandeep Kumar] and his two friends Neema and Kulbir Singh {first cousin}, were -4- 2024:HHC:4510 attending a marriage function-reception of another friend, Neeraj at Village Bhattiyan along with villagers and relatives [including ladies] and were having food at about . 09:00 p.m., on 20.01.2024, then, persons, namely, Amit, Hoshiar Singh and Kalveer Singh, Rajeev Kumar and Jatinder Singh [bail petitioners herein] entered the marriage spot and reached inside the tent, in their open Jonga vehicle, bearing registration No HP-12K-9792, where ladies were dancing on the DJ. On this, the complainant [Sandeep Kumar] and his two friends requested them not to resort to unwarranted activities. After persistent requests, the bail petitioners left the marriage spot but by threatening the complainant and his friends with dire consequences. 3(i). After leaving the marriage reception, accused persons, parked their Jonga vehicle, HP-12K-9792 about -5- 2024:HHC:4510 50 Meters away from the marriage spot, near the house of Rajeev [one of the bail petitioners in Cr.MP(M) No.919 of 2024], where a Fortuner having registration No HP-12G- . 3535, was parked on the road. The status report reveals that the police recorded the Statements under Section 161 Cr.P.C of the complainant [Sandeep Kumar] and his friend Kulbir on 22.01.2024 and the statement of another friend, Neema, was recorded on 29.01.2024. 5(vi). The status report reveals that the "Sword" used by Rajeev and Jatinder was recovered by the police. It further indicates that after dismissal of bail petitions in cases of six bail petitioners on 24.05.2024; five accused [except Satish Kumar, Up Pradhan] surrendered on 27.05.2024 and pursuant to disclosures made during remand on 28.05.2024, the "Drat" used by accused-Amit was recovered on 28.05.2024 by the police. 5(vii). Status Report filed by the State Authorities reveals that due to use of Sword, the accusation under - 13 - 2024:HHC:4510 Section 25-54-59 of Arms Act was added to the FIR. It further narrates that the Final Police Report points towards the accusation under Sections 307, 147, 148, 149, . 323 and 506 IPC, which has been forwarded/presented before the jurisdictional Court on 19.04.2024. Though originally the FIR No.14 of 2024 dated 20.1.2024 was registered under Sections 147, 148, 149, 323 and 506 IPC, but keeping in view the medical opinion, gravity of offence, the nature of injuries inflicted which were grievous in nature and dangerous to life, therefore, Section 307 IPC was inserted/ added to the aforesaid FIR on 20.02.2024 and in this background, the bail applications filed by the present bail petitioners were dismissed by Learned Trial Court i.e. Additional Sessions Judge, Nalagarh, on 01.03.2024 [Annexure P-1], in following terms, which reads as under:- "10. The allegations against the bail applicant is that he along with his accomplices caused injuries to the complainant and his other two friends by beating them with sickle, swords and also fired a gun shot in the air to intimidate them. This incident was preceded by verbal altercation in the house of - 21 - 2024:HHC:4510 marriage of Mr. Neeraj. The fact that thereafter, when bail applicant and their accomplices assembled near the place of marriage with the aforementioned weapons and waited for complainant and his friends clearly implies that bail . applicant and his accomplices had made complete plan to attack complainant and other two boys and to intimidate them. They caused serious injuries to the complainant as evident from the final opinion of the Doctor. On entering the tent, the accused started making obscene remarks and unwarranted acts by resorting to continuous dippering the head flasher lights of the Jonga, which was objected to by the complainant, along with his two friends but after persistent requests, the occupants of the Jonga [driven by bail petitioners, Jatinder Singh with Rajeev Kumar, on the side seat along with others], left the scene of occurrence by threatening the complainant and his friends of dire consequences. After attending the marriage party reception, as soon - 25 - 2024:HHC:4510 as the complainant [Sandeep Kumar] along with his two friends, namely, Neema and Kulbir were on way home, on 20.01.2024 at about 10.00 p.m. and were about to . cross the road from the frontside of these vehicles, then, they were mercilessly attacked by accused persons, whereby the bail petitioners, Rajeev and Jatinder attacked the complainant with "Sword" and another accused-Amit attacked the complainant(s) by hurling blows by a "Drat" on the head of complainant-Sandeep Kumar. Notably, the third bail petitioner, Kulveer along with other accused gave beatings to all the three injured persons. Moreover, a perusal of the Medical Records of CHC Nalagarh i.e. [Government Hospital], indicates . that the complainant [Sandeep Kumar] was admitted to this CHC on 21.01.2024 at 12:10 a.m., and due to merciless attack by the accused persons, including the bail petitioners, the complainant-Sandeep Kumar sustained fracture on the cerebral hemisphere on left parietal bone which was detected in CT scan. This CT scan report was sent to IGMC, Shimla, [a premier health institution of the State at Shimla] for medical opinion, who opined on 24.01.2024, that the injury is grievous in nature. However, on 17.02.2024, the Investigating Officer, Police Post, Dhabota, Tehsil Nalagarh, District Solan, wrote a letter to Medical Officer, seeking opinion as to whether the injury sustained was dangerous to life or not? After taking into account all the medical records including the opinion of IGMC Shimla, the Medical Officer, CHC Nalagarh finally opined that the injuries sustained by complainant [Sandeep - 29 - 2024:HHC:4510 Kumar], were dangerous to life and based on this opinion, Section 307 IPC was added to the FIR. Not only the complainant-Sandeep Kumar . but two of his friends namely, Neema and Kulbir, were medically examined, who also sustained simple injuries.
texts.arguments: This contention of Learned Senior Counsel is without merit, for the reason, that firstly, the overt act/incident was done with the intention to cause hurt-injury by using deadly weapons; and secondly, the medical reports suggest that the injuries inflicted are dangerous to life; and thirdly, for the purpose of - 32 - 2024:HHC:4510 involving Section 307 IPC, the nature of injury being grievous or life threatening or fatal was not necessary; and lastly, the ambit and scope of Section 307 of Indian . Penal Code has been mandated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, State of Madhya Pradesh versus Saleem, (2005) 5 SCC 554, Jage Ram versus State of Haryana, (2015) 11 SCC 366 and State of Madhya Pradesh versus Kanha, (2019) 3 SCC 605, that if an act, irrespective of its result was done, with the intention or knowledge or under circumstances mentioned in the Section then, the grievous or life threatening injury was not necessary to maintain-invoke accusation under Section 307 IPC and such an intention can be ascertained from the actual injury, surrounding circumstances and nature of weapon used and severity of blows inflicted by an accused. On facts of this case, as borne out from the Status Report and the other material on record, the prima facie accusation is made out under Section 307 IPC, revealing their preparedness to commit offence, Rajeev Kumar vs State Of Himachal Pradesh on 4 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136364644/ 15 - 33 - 2024:HHC:4510 carrying deadly weapons assembling together at one place near two of their parked vehicles; giving effect to their premeditated mind/intention by causing mercilessly . attacks by Drat and Sword; leading to fracture on the Cerebral hemisphere on left parietal bone [borne out from MLC], and recovery of the Drat and Sword by the State Authorities at instance of the bail petitioners No.1 & 3 herein on 28.05.2024 points towards the prima-facie accusation, which dissuades this Court from enlarging the petitioners on bail, at this stage, in view of the grave and serious offence attributable to the petitioners. 15. On considering the pros and cons of the respective contentions of Learned Senior Counsel as well as Learned State Counsel, this Court is of the considered view, that the accusation contained in FIR No.14 of 2024, - 38 - 2024:HHC:4510 dated 20.01.2024, under Section 307 IPC is not cognizable by a Gram Panchayat, by virtue of Schedule-III to Section 32 of the Himachal Pradesh Panchayati Raj Act, . 1994. Even, under the Himachal Pradesh Gram Panchayati Raj Act, the Gram Panchayat has no power to compound the offence under Section 307 IPC.
